questions.answer: The country and culture

questions.answer: fairly easy

questions.answer: none

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Farily easy, I searched for co-living and found a lot of nice things

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice, I think if you live on campus you tend to live in a bubble and not experience the city as much

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very easy. I did not get accepted at the department relevant for my filed of studies and ended up being registred as an undergraduate even though I am a graduate. This meant that there were certain courses I could not take at graduate level....

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you have to apply to a department, though I don't think it matters a lot which one since I did not take courses at the department I ended up being registred at, since it did not match my major at all. The process was though a bit confusing. Also the course list they attached from the last year, did not match the courses they offered when I was there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: one person of contact at the host university on mail

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: semi, there were some graduate courses I wanted that I could not take, since I was registered as an undergraduate student (even though I am a graduate student at KU).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: try the rehearsal, since the process is a bit confusing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was alright, a bit easier. I had only european professors plus one from Canada, so similar to what I am used to. Though a lot more student involvement/presentations than I am used to and attendance is mandatory.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: a lot more student involvement

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Seminar in geopolitics, comparative politics, studies in modern asian civilisations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the course on geopolitics very interesting

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy I think, but I have also lived in Japan which is similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: SNU Buddy

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No one speaks English, but with a translation app it is very easy. people are generally very friendly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: remember physical credit cards!!! They don't take Apple Pay at many places, which makes it impossible to pay many places without a physical card. Also the card is ofen times rejected, so important with more cards, so you can try different ones. it was the same for many of the other Danes. so alway carry a bit of cash also.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: the registration process, and that there aren't many English taught courses at graduate level

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: experiencing a different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: a lot of things were difficult because everything is in korean. also the university website is all in korean almost... makes it difficult to find information

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would though definitely recommend Korea!! such a fascinating country!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
